feed.title: Google Cloud: Memorystore for Redis Cluster
feed.subtitle: Changelog for Google Cloud product: Memorystore for Redis Cluster

entry.content: You can use access control list (ACL) policies to secure access to your clusters. You can enable fine-grained security by restricting user and service access to specific keys, commands, operations, and Pub/Sub channels. This feature is Generally Available.
entry.summary: Enhance your Memorystore cluster security with access control list (ACL) policies. This feature, now Generally Available, allows for fine-grained control over user and service access to specific keys, commands, and operations, ensuring robust data protection.
entry.title: Feature: Secure your Memorystore clusters with ACL policies

entry.content: You can use the Google Cloud console to secure access to your clusters by using basic token-based authentication. This feature is available in Preview.
entry.summary: You can now secure access to your clusters using basic token-based authentication. This new feature, available in Preview, can be managed through the Google Cloud console.
entry.title: Feature: Secure cluster access with basic authentication

entry.content: The customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) feature for Memorystore for Redis Cluster is now Generally Available.
entry.summary: We are pleased to announce that Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for Memorystore for Redis Cluster is now Generally Available. This feature allows you to manage your own encryption keys for enhanced security.
entry.title: Feature: Memorystore for Redis Cluster Now Supports CMEK
